Definition: A product or services technology company occupying space for its own staff — engineering, product, support and the business functions around them.
Signature spaces: Dense open workhall; high meeting-room-to-seat ratio; phone booths at scale; war rooms; large cafeteria doubling as town hall
What it drives in the deck: Hybrid AV in every room, and a defensible desk-sharing ratio. Attendance data is the argument, not an aside.
Watch out for: Engineering-heavy audiences distrust mood boards without plans; lead with capacity and adjacency, not materials.

Definition: A captive offshore centre delivering work for a foreign parent. The occupier is a subsidiary; the standards usually are not theirs to set.
Signature spaces: Shift-based workhall; follow-the-sun collaboration rooms aligned to parent time zones; town hall; large cafeteria; transport lobby
What it drives in the deck: Conformance to the parent's global workplace standard is the spine of the deck. Every deviation must be shown and justified, and the deck will be reviewed by people who are not in the country.
Audience: India site lead + global workplace standards team + parent RE
Watch out for: The deck is read asynchronously overseas, so it must stand alone without a presenter — notes and annotations matter more than usual.

Definition: An early or fast-scaling company where headcount at handover is a guess and the workplace is part of the hiring pitch.
Signature spaces: Flexible open plan; almost no cabins; one all-hands space; café-as-workspace; a founder-visible war room
What it drives in the deck: Growth headroom and cost per seat. The plan must visibly survive a 40% headcount swing in either direction.
Audience: Founder / COO, deciding fast and often alone
Watch out for: Short attention, fast decisions. A 50-slide deck loses this client; compress process slides into one.

Definition: A coworking or managed-workspace operator fitting out a centre they will sub-let. The people in the space are not the client's staff.
Signature spaces: Sellable private cabins at several sizes; hot-desk lounge; community / event space; premium meeting suites let by the hour; phone booths
What it drives in the deck: Sellable seats per sq ft and revenue mix are the argument. Design is evaluated as a yield instrument, not as taste.
Watch out for: Brand must stay neutral enough to host any tenant. Resist client-specific storytelling that a future tenant cannot inherit.

Definition: An operator builds and runs the space, but a single named client occupies all of it and expects it to feel like theirs.
Signature spaces: Client-branded reception; standard workhall; operator back-of-house; housekeeping and pantry ops zones
What it drives in the deck: Two audiences at once: the operator (who must run it) and the tenant (who must love it). Operations, SLA and BOH earn real slide time here and almost nowhere else.
Audience: Operator delivery team + the end client's workplace lead
Watch out for: Ownership of change requests after handover is the most common dispute — cover it explicitly.

Definition: Banking, financial services or insurance — regulated, audited, and usually client-facing on at least one floor.
Signature spaces: Dealing / trading floor; client meeting suite segregated from staff areas; secure records; compliance-restricted zones; formal boardroom
What it drives in the deck: Security zoning and regulatory segregation are design drivers, not an annexe. Access hierarchy gets its own slide.
Watch out for: Compliance sign-off can veto a plan late. Show the restricted-zone logic before the pretty renders.

Definition: Consulting, audit, accountancy or advisory — high-salary staff who are mostly at a client site, and a client suite that must impress.
Signature spaces: Hotelling desks with booking; client-facing meeting suite; partner cabins; quiet rooms; project/war rooms
What it drives in the deck: Low real attendance against high headcount. Desk-sharing ratio is the commercial argument, and the client suite is the brand argument.
Watch out for: Partners will negotiate cabin entitlement individually. Make the hierarchy rule explicit and visual early.

Definition: Law firms and chambers — cellular by nature, confidentiality-bound, and materially conservative.
Signature spaces: Cellular offices; library / archive; secure file storage; formal reception and client waiting; deposition / conference rooms
What it drives in the deck: Acoustic privacy is a legal requirement, not a comfort preference. Open-plan proposals need a defence.
Watch out for: Do not lead with open-plan or ABW. Show the acoustic strategy before proposing any shared setting.

Definition: The corporate office of an e-commerce, quick-commerce or logistics business — operations-led, often running around the clock.
Signature spaces: Control tower / ops floor with screen wall; large war rooms; 24x7 zones with their own pantry and rest area; high-turnover cafeteria
What it drives in the deck: Peak-season surge capacity and genuine 24x7 operation. The plan has to work at 3am on the busiest night of the year.
Watch out for: Shift overlap doubles occupancy at handover times — size circulation and amenities for the overlap, not the average.

Definition: Corporate and R&D-adjacent offices for healthcare, pharma or life sciences organisations, under regulated conditions.
Signature spaces: Controlled-access document and sample storage; clean-adjacent corridors; wellness rooms; training auditorium; visitor segregation
What it drives in the deck: Regulated adjacency and material hygiene. Finishes are selected for cleanability and certification before appearance.
Watch out for: Quality/Regulatory can reject a specified finish outright. Get the material schedule in front of them early.

Definition: An engineering, semiconductor or hardware R&D centre where labs and office space share a floor plate and an IP boundary.
Signature spaces: Lab / office interface zone; prototype and test areas; secure IP zones; heavy-services rooms; equipment staging and goods route
What it drives in the deck: The lab boundary governs everything: services load, vibration, access control and the goods route all precede aesthetics.
Watch out for: Services capacity is usually the binding constraint. Confirm it before committing to any lab adjacency.

Definition: A corporate office attached to or serving a plant — office staff and plant staff share entrances, canteens and a safety culture.
Signature spaces: Office-to-plant transition and PPE zone; visitor safety induction room; shared canteen; training rooms; durable circulation
What it drives in the deck: The office/plant interface and the safety induction sequence. Durability beats delicacy in every material call.
Watch out for: Plant staff and office staff have different expectations of the same canteen. Show both journeys, not an averaged one.

Definition: Agencies, production houses, and direct-to-consumer brands where the office is itself a brand artefact and often a shoot location.
Signature spaces: Shoot / content studio; edit suites with acoustic treatment; product and sample display; informal-first collaboration; a photographable hero moment
What it drives in the deck: The office doubles as a set and a showroom. Lighting quality and photogenic moments are functional requirements here.
Watch out for: This audience out-designs most decks in their own field. Show restraint and craft; generic corporate renders read as lazy.

Definition: Offices for education providers and EdTech companies, usually with teaching, recording or assembly space on the same floor.
Signature spaces: Classroom / lab hybrid rooms; recording studios; large assembly space; counselling and admissions rooms; student waiting
What it drives in the deck: Peak assembly load and acoustic separation between teaching and recording. Durability under heavy young footfall.
Watch out for: Timetable peaks, not headcount, size the circulation and the washrooms. Ask for the timetable.

Definition: Public-sector, PSU and institutional offices — hierarchical, tender-governed and open to the public.
Signature spaces: Rank-allocated cabins; public interface and grievance counter; records room; committee and conference rooms; public waiting
What it drives in the deck: Entitlement norms and tender compliance define the plan before design begins. Deviation needs written justification.
Watch out for: Cabin sizes are often fixed by published norms. Confirm the applicable schedule before planning anything.

Definition: A briefing centre, innovation hub or showcase space whose purpose is to be visited rather than worked in.
Signature spaces: Narrative visitor journey; demo and immersion zones; AV-led feature walls; hospitality and VIP lounge; a briefing theatre
What it drives in the deck: The visitor's route IS the design. Sequence, dwell time and reveal order carry more slides than desking ever will.
Watch out for: Content and AV are usually a separate vendor on a different timeline. Fix the interface early or it derails handover.
